items.title: Reconcile the frozen contract parallel-decomposition.ts to re-export the REAL impls (replace the 3 NotImplemented skeletons computeWriteSet/globsOverlap/evaluateDecompositionGate)
items.context: core/parallel-decomposition.ts currently THROWS 'NotImplemented' for computeWriteSet (lines ~68-71), globsOverlap (~77-81), evaluateDecompositionGate (~88-99). Replace each with a re-export of the real impl: `export { computeWriteSet, globsOverlap } from './parallel-decomposition-overlap.js'` and `export { evaluateDecompositionGate } from './parallel-decomposition-gate.js'`. The contract's TYPES (ParallelGateConfig/GlobOverlapResult/DecompositionGateResult/ParallelDecompositionBlock) stay defined here and are still imported (type-only) by the impl modules — type-only imports are erased at runtime so there is no runtime cycle. No current caller imports the functions from the contract (they import directly from -overlap.js/-gate.js), so the re-export is non-breaking; optionally migrate those importers to the contract path IF it stays clean (no circular-import breakage), else leave them.

happy.desc: importing computeWriteSet/globsOverlap/evaluateDecompositionGate from core/parallel-decomposition.js returns the REAL functions (computeWriteSet on a contract returns its write-set; globsOverlap detects an overlap; evaluateDecompositionGate returns {advisories,block}) — NOT a NotImplemented throw; WHY: the frozen contract now re-exports the real impls

edge.desc: the contract still EXPORTS the types (ParallelGateConfig/GlobOverlapResult/DecompositionGateResult/ParallelDecompositionBlock) and the tsc build is clean (no circular-import runtime break); WHY: type-only imports by the impl modules must not create a runtime cycle

adversarial.desc: no caller is broken by the re-export: full lattice validate (all configured smokes + build) stays green; WHY: re-export must be non-breaking for every existing importer

items.title: Wire evaluateDecompositionGate into canStartDevGuard (machine.ts) as a FAIL-OPEN hard-block sub-check, enforcing the block ONLY under parallelGate.mode==='block'
items.context: core/machine.ts canStartDevGuard (~lines 299-317) is the REAL PLAN->DEV decision oracle (returns boolean; the outer try/catch is fail-CLOSED for the review gate). After the existing review-clean check, add the parallel-decomposition sub-check in its OWN nested try/catch that is FAIL-OPEN (on ANY error, fall through to allow — do NOT return false; spec §4.8: a gate/config infra error must never block PLAN->DEV). Inside: resolve cfg = resolveAuditConfig(policy.profile, projectRoot).parallelGate; only when cfg.mode==='block' load peers (store.listStoryIds().filter(!==self).map(readStory)) + contracts (safeReadScopeContract per id, non-null only), call evaluateDecompositionGate(story, peers, contracts, cfg), and return false ONLY if gateResult.block!==null. mode 'advise'/'off' => never blocks here (advisory is Story 4's surface). Use policy.profile (from resolveWorkflowPolicy) for the profile, consistent with story-review.

happy.desc: canStartDevGuard returns FALSE for a story asserting parallelSafe=yes whose write-set tier-1 overlaps an active parallel peer, when parallelGate.mode=block and the review is otherwise clean; WHY: the hard block fires under mode=block on a provable overlap
canStartDevGuard returns TRUE for a clean disjoint wave (no overlap) with mode=block and a clean review; WHY: the gate must not block provably-independent work

edge.desc: the SAME overlapping configuration returns TRUE (allowed) under mode=advise AND under mode=off; WHY: advise/off never hard-block — only mode=block enforces
canStartDevGuard still returns FALSE when the review is unclean/missing (existing fail-closed review gate unchanged), independent of the parallel sub-check; WHY: no regression of the existing guard

adversarial.desc: FAIL-OPEN: when the parallel sub-check throws (e.g. a parallelGate config that makes resolveAuditConfig/peer-load throw) and the review is clean, canStartDevGuard returns TRUE (allows DEV); WHY: a gate/config infra error must never strand PLAN->DEV (spec 4.8)

an unreadable peer scope-contract under mode=block yields the gate block (peer_contract_unreadable_parallel) -> guard returns false (refuse the parallel assertion per 4.8 corrupt-peer fail-closed), NOT a crash; WHY: the corrupt-peer bypass is closed without crashing

items.title: Mirror the block reason in getGuardFailureReason (machine.ts) so the PLAN->DEV failure message explains the parallel-decomposition block
items.context: core/machine.ts getGuardFailureReason targetPhase==='DEV' branch (~lines 653-719) must render a human-readable reason for the same block canStartDevGuard enforces, keeping the two in sync. Add (mirroring the same mode==='block' + peers/contracts + evaluateDecompositionGate computation) a branch that, when gateResult.block!==null, returns 'Cannot enter DEV: <actionable message per block reason>' naming the colliding peer/path where available. Wrap in try/catch that on error returns null/falls through (do not fabricate a block message on a gate error). The block-reason->message mapping should be a small shared helper so canStartDevGuard's decision and this message derive from the same predicate.

happy.desc: for the same blocked config (overlap, mode=block, clean review) getGuardFailureReason(storyId,store,DEV,root) returns a non-null string containing the actionable block reason naming the colliding peer/path; WHY: the operator sees WHY DEV was refused

edge.desc: for a clean/allowed wave getGuardFailureReason returns null for the parallel sub-check (no phantom message); WHY: a message must appear only when the guard actually blocks

decision/message PARITY: whenever canStartDevGuard returns false due to the parallel block, getGuardFailureReason returns a non-null parallel message, and when the guard allows, no parallel message is produced — both derived from the one shared helper; WHY: decision and reason must not drift

adversarial.desc: getGuardFailureReason FAILS OPEN on a gate sub-check error: when the parallel sub-check throws, it returns null (no fabricated block message) rather than throwing; WHY: a gate infra error must not produce a phantom refusal message or crash the reason renderer

items.title: Hermetic smoke proving the hard gate end-to-end: parallel overlap BLOCKS under mode=block, broad glob blocks (strict), clean disjoint passes, mode=off/advise do NOT block, config/gate-infra failure FAILS OPEN, unreadable peer contract under block refuses the parallel assertion
items.context: New packages/main/src/tasks/parallel-decomposition-gate-integration-smoke.ts (follow the evidence-state-gate-smoke.ts temp-repo pattern OR a hermetic mock-store pattern). Assert canStartDevGuard returns false for a tier-1 declared-parallel overlap under mode=block; returns true for the same under mode=advise and mode=off; returns true for a clean disjoint wave; FAILS OPEN (returns true) when the gate sub-check throws (e.g. a config that makes resolveAuditConfig/peer-load throw); and getGuardFailureReason returns a message naming the block for the blocked case and null for the clean case. Register in lattice.config.json.

happy.desc: the integration smoke runs green proving: overlap+mode=block -> canStartDevGuard false + getGuardFailureReason non-null naming the block; clean disjoint -> true + null; WHY: end-to-end proof the hard gate works and the message matches

edge.desc: smoke asserts mode=advise and mode=off both allow the same overlap (guard true), and a missing/unclean review still blocks via the existing gate; WHY: mode semantics + no regression proven end-to-end

adversarial.desc: smoke asserts FAIL-OPEN: a parallelGate config that makes the sub-check throw -> canStartDevGuard true and getGuardFailureReason null (with the review otherwise clean); WHY: the single most important property (infra error never blocks) is proven, not just asserted
smoke is registered in lattice.config.json validate.commands and lattice validate stays all-green; WHY: the gate test runs in CI on every validate
